list.desc: At PlanRadar, selecting a row in a large list re-rendered every row via array-identity comparison — O(n²). I swapped it for a Set-membership lookup, so only the touched row re-renders. Click rows below.
list.note: // Old: full list re-renders on every selection. New: only the touched row updates.

storage.desc: Migrated PlanRadar's persistence from AsyncStorage to MMKV — synchronous, encrypted, faster reads.
storage.note: // MMKV writes are synchronous — no await, no flicker on read.

sync.desc: One of PlanRadar's core modules is offline-first and real-time over WebSockets — actions queue while offline and flush on reconnect. Toggle offline below and make changes.
sync.note: // Queued actions flush in order once the socket reconnects.

firebase.desc: Firebase underpins observability on both PlanRadar and Index Group apps — Analytics for usage tracking, Crashlytics for crash-free-rate monitoring, and FCM as the transport for push. Trigger an SDK call below.
firebase.note: // Crashlytics context (user id, breadcrumbs) is set before the throw, not after — otherwise the report arrives with no idea what led up to it.

restapi.desc: PlanRadar and Index Group both talk to the backend over a typed REST/JSON:API layer — an Axios client with interceptors for auth-token attach, 401 refresh, and centralized error normalization, wrapped in resource hooks components call directly. Fetch below to trace the pipeline.
restapi.note: // The request interceptor shares one in-flight refresh across concurrent 401s instead of racing a refresh per request.

anim.desc: Reanimated / Animated API drives modal and navigation transitions at PlanRadar. Two examples below.
anim.note: // Reanimated worklets run on the UI thread — no JS-thread jank under load.

deeplink.desc: At Index Group, notifications and shared links opened the app directly to a specific order or driver screen.
deeplink.note: // Unmatched paths fall back to a default route instead of crashing the navigator.

ulink.desc: Universal Links (iOS) and App Links (Android) skip the custom-scheme prompt entirely — a real https:// link opens the app directly if it's installed, or the web page if not.
ulink.note: // No installed app → same URL opens the mobile web fallback instead.

push.desc: Push notifications via FCM, wired to deep links so tapping one routes straight to the relevant screen.
push.note: // getInitialNotification() covers the cold-start case FCM's foreground handler misses.

cicd.desc: Full release ownership at PlanRadar and Index Group — GitLab CI/CD, EAS Build, TestFlight, and Play Console. Run the pipeline below.
cicd.note: // Same pipeline shape across both apps: test → build → submit, gated on green tests.

i18n.desc: Multi-locale support via i18next and react-native-localize, including RTL for Arabic.
i18n.note: // react-native-localize detects device locale; I18nManager flips layout direction.

newarch.desc: Led PlanRadar's migration to React Native 0.85 — Hermes + New Architecture. JSI replaces the old async, JSON-serialized bridge with direct synchronous native calls. Click to compare.
newarch.note: // JSI gives JS a direct reference to native objects — no serialize/queue/deserialize round trip.

release.desc: Co-architected RN's packaging as a versioned native binary (XCFramework + AAR) — decoupling the RN layer from native host apps, no Node/Yarn toolchain required for native teams.
release.note: // Native teams bump one version string — no RN toolchain install, no Metro, no Yarn.

testing.desc: 1,500+ commits across 200+ tickets at PlanRadar, guarded by a 3,500+ test suite in GitLab CI/CD. Run a sample suite.
testing.note: // CI blocks merge on red tests — coverage gate keeps refactors safe across 200+ tickets.

ota.desc: CodePush OTA delivery at Index Group — ship JS/asset updates without an app-store review cycle, staged and reversible.
ota.note: // Bad bundle at any stage → rollback reverts devices to the last known-good version.

tv.desc: Extending React Native to Smart TV — tvOS and Android TV via react-native-tvos — swaps touch for D-pad focus navigation. No shipped production app yet — architecture below is how I'd approach it.
tv.note: // Same component model, different input system — focus/spatial nav replaces touch gestures.

wearables.desc: Wearables (watchOS, Wear OS) pair over a native companion bridge, not a shrunk-down RN screen — both directions. No shipped production app yet — architecture below is how I'd approach it.
wearables.note: // The bridge is native-to-native — RN only sends/receives the payload, the watch app renders it.

aiassistant.desc: PlanRadar's in-app AI Assistant — I built the RN client: WebSocket-streamed staged responses (thinking → response), ticket/document context attachments, and usage-tier gating. Architecture below, renamed from the real implementation. Pick a prompt below.
aiassistant.note: // Streamed over WebSockets, not polled — the thinking stage renders while the model is still working.

gesture.desc: A physics-based swipe stack — spring return, velocity-aware flick-to-dismiss, and rubber-band rotation. Drag the front card.
gesture.note: // Direct DOM mutation during drag, React state only touches on release — no re-render per frame.

nodeapi.desc: Backend work isn't limited to consuming REST APIs from the RN client — I've also built and maintained Node.js/Express services, with an authenticated middleware pipeline in front of the business logic. Run it below.
nodeapi.note: // Each middleware either calls next() or ends the response — the controller only runs once every gate passes.

reactweb.desc: Beyond React Native, I work with React.js and Next.js fundamentals — this portfolio itself is one example. Below: how a page goes from a server-rendered response to fully interactive, via hydration.
reactweb.note: // The server sends real HTML immediately — hydration attaches event listeners to it, it doesn't re-render from scratch.
